clue.text: Great works of a number of races

definitions.meaning: enduring masterpieces of literature, music or art
the five English flat races for three-year-olds, such as the Derby and the Oaks, are collectively so called

explanation.surface: A commentator praises some celebrated races as great works.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: timeless works of art, and Britain's five premier horse races for three-year-olds.

clue.text: Famous people seen around Eastern island

indicators.note: around means the famous people enclose the letter for Eastern

parts.note: celebs is short for celebrities

explanation.surface: Celebrities are spotted on an island in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Celebes is the former name of Sulawesi, an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebes is the old name of Sulawesi, a large island in Indonesia.

clue.text: Vestment almost completely black? On the contrary!

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for completely is lost

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all wet'
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A priest's robe described as nearly all black, then the opposite insisted on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' tells you to read 'almost completely' as one piece, not 'completely black': AL then B. It also teases, since the alb is a white robe.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a white linen vestment reaching to the feet, worn by clergy at Mass.

clue.text: A grouser's pique, initially, could result in these

definitions.text: A grouser's pique, initially, could result in these

indicators.note: says the preceding letters could be turned into another arrangement
initially takes the first letter of pique

explanation.surface: A complainer's resentment may give rise to a dismissive attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could result in' rearranges A GROUSERS plus P (initially, from pique); the whole clue describes the result too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is resentful disparagement of something one cannot have, which a grouser's pique produces.

clue.text: A couple of Greek letters delivered in African capital

indicators.note: delivered as in spoken, so the letters are said out loud

parts.note: chi and rho, the pair forming the Christian monogram, pronounced 'kye-roe'

explanation.surface: Two Greek letters are posted to a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' suggests post, but here means spoken: chi rho said out loud sounds like the Egyptian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt, in Africa.

clue.text: University publication is student's work

parts.note: THES is the Times Higher Education Supplement, a weekly paper about universities
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university paper is said to be the product of a student's labour.
explanation.walkthrough: THES, the Times Higher Education Supplement, is a British weekly covering universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation written for a degree is a student's major piece of work.

clue.text: Given cards as worker

definitions.meaning: the set of cards dealt to a player

explanation.surface: A labourer is dealt a set of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is the cards a player holds, and also a hired labourer.

clue.text: Airlines flying over the capital of island

indicators.note: over means the rearranged letters arch over and enclose the next word
flying suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Planes fly over the main town of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' is the anagram signal and 'over' the container signal. St Helier is the capital of Jersey, one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helier is the capital of Jersey, a Channel Island.

clue.text: Cook one way, a limited way, as caterer

parts.note: stewing is one way to cook
RD, a road cut short to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A caterer cooks in one manner and has restricted options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' signals the shortened form RD of road.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward manages food and drink on a ship, plane or in a club, a kind of caterer.

clue.text: Partnership soundly believes in provision for emergencies

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen

indicators.note: soundly means the next word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: buys means accepts as true, as in 'I don't buy that'

explanation.surface: A firm partnership holds faith in its emergency plans.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket stand is a run-scoring partnership. BUYS (believes in) said out loud gives BYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Standbys are reserves kept ready for use in an emergency.

clue.text: Needing lots of workers, unlike today's Scotland?

definitions.meaning: describes an industry that relies on much manual effort
read as a phrase about politics: Scotland is no longer heavily dominated by the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A remark comparing old industrial demands with modern Scottish politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: Labour, once dominant in Scotland, has lost much ground there, so the country is no longer full of Labour support.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes work requiring a large workforce, and punningly a place packed with Labour Party voters.

clue.text: Part of defence pulverized — it's history

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby
ground means crushed to powder

explanation.surface: A football report says part of the defence was crushed and is now consigned to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's background is their past history and experience.

clue.text: One may get a good deal behind another vehicle here

definitions.text: One may get a good deal behind another vehicle here

parts.words: One may get a good deal behind another vehicle here
parts.note: a bargain may be had from goods laid out at the back of someone else's car

explanation.surface: Advice about getting a good trade-in at a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain people sell second-hand goods from their car boots, the British word for a car's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A car boot sale is a British market where people sell goods from the backs of their cars.

clue.text: Architectural feature specifically that of Athens, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the starting letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A guide talks of a building feature belonging particularly to ancient Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of 'specifically that of Athens'; the stoa was indeed a famous Athenian colonnade.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered colonnade or portico, typical of ancient Greek public buildings, is an architectural feature.

clue.text: A limited number left — sign displayed for ladies

parts.note: NO, number cut short to its abbreviation
blew means left hurriedly, as in 'blew town'
an omen is a sign of the future

explanation.surface: Only a few remain, a notice shown for women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like L but is the slang verb for leaving fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies in the formal sense are women of noble rank.

clue.text: Batman and Robin, initially with vehicle in movie location

indicators.note: in means the letters from Robin and the vehicle are placed within the movie location

parts.note: a set is where a film is shot

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Robin

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Batman and Robin turn up with their car on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batman' is not the comic-book hero but an officer's personal attendant in the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is a soldier acting as an officer's personal attendant, a kind of manservant.

clue.text: Moving with beat, i.e. dancing

parts.note: tan means to beat, as in 'tan his hide'
going means moving

explanation.surface: Moving in rhythm, that is, dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means doing the tango, which is dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangoing is performing the tango, a form of dancing.

clue.text: Next to the Bible, it'll keep up the good work

definitions.text: Next to the Bible, it'll keep up the good work

parts.words: Next to the Bible, it'll keep up the good work
parts.note: something standing beside the Good Book on a shelf holds the volume upright; 'keep up the good work' is read literally

explanation.surface: Encouragement to carry on doing good, as if from a preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock phrase 'keep up the good work' becomes literal: a support that keeps a book (the Good Book) standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookend is a support placed at the end of a row of books to keep them upright.

clue.text: New composition for a tenor with piano, having many variations

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: a new composition is a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer writes a new piece for tenor and piano, full of variations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New composition for' rearranges A TENOR into ROTEAN, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Protean means taking many forms, after the shape-shifting sea god Proteus.

clue.text: Piece of music -—- it's in the first section

indicators.note: in means the word it is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a part is a section
A is the first letter, as in A1
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of music is placed in its opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a suite of instrumental pieces, as by Bach.

clue.text: Serve a piece of toast

definitions.meaning: a finger of toast for dipping in a boiled egg, in British usage

explanation.surface: An instruction at breakfast to serve up some toast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a strip of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg is called by this military name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to serve as a fighter, and in British homes is a strip of toast for egg dipping.

clue.text: Fruit on wild plant grew with it

parts.note: rose means grew, went up
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Fruit on a wild plant that grew along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosehip is the red fruit of the wild rose.

clue.text: Girl Keats equated with beauty, though not the first time

indicators.note: says the first letter is dropped, which here is also T for time

parts.note: Keats wrote 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty' in Ode on a Grecian Urn

explanation.surface: A girl whom the poet Keats likened to beauty, though not on the first occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first time' removes the opening T (time) from TRUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's name, as of the biblical heroine.

clue.text: Badly thrown when crossing road to Scotland, say

indicators.note: badly means the letters are thrown into disorder
crossing means the word for when goes either side of the road

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something hurled carelessly while crossing a road on the way to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' is the anagram signal; 'crossing' puts one piece around another. 'Scotland, say' is just one example of a northerly destination from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies to the north of England, so heading there is going in a northerly direction.

clue.text: Slightly adjust temperature, then faint

parts.note: weak means faint, feeble

explanation.surface: Turn the thermostat a touch, then feel weak.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make a fine adjustment.

clue.text: Told stories in song

definitions.meaning: told untruths, as with 'telling stories' to a teacher
a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: Someone told tales through music.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie is to tell stories, and a Lied is a German art song.

clue.text: It's at home in virtual reconstruction

definitions.note: read as 'It is': It is the short name for a sweet Italian aperitif, as in 'gin and it'

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds something in new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that something feels at home in virtual reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstruction' rearranges all fifteen letters of AT HOME IN VIRTUAL. 'It' is the old bar name for the drink in 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: In bar slang 'It' is short for the vermouth from Italy, so the drink is It.

clue.text: Instrument in this state needing another key

parts.note: for a British newspaper this country is the UK
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An instrument in a poor state needs another key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this state' is the UK, from the setter's British viewpoint; a uke is a ukulele.
explanation.definitionFit: A uke is short for ukulele, a small four-stringed instrument.

clue.text: In Copenhagen, Danes set programme for meeting

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Danish officials in Copenhagen draw up the schedule for a conference.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Superficial type put in place of bishop with power

indicators.note: put in means the type word goes inside the bishop's place

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese or seat
kind means type
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A shallow sort of person installed where a bishop should be, given authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-deep describes something only on the surface, like beauty, so shallow.
